title: Stereotaxic Surgery for In Vivo Extracellular Recording at Rat Schaffer Collateral-CA1 Synapse
author: Azimzadeh, Mohd Azmi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare animal and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Inject urethane; anesthesia should appear within 1–5 min. If insufficient, give an additional dose equal to one‑tenth of the initial injection. Maintain anesthesia for the whole surgery (typically 3–4 h). Monitor breathing rhythm, tail‑toe pinch reflex, heart rate and internal temperature throughout.

steps.title: Position rat in stereotaxic frame
steps.instruction: Secure the rat in the stereotaxic apparatus, ensure the head is level, and locate bregma. Record the anterior‑posterior (AP) and mediolateral (ML) coordinates using a guide cannula.

steps.title: Determine target coordinates
steps.instruction: Using the guide cannula, lower it along the dorsoventral (DV) axis until it contacts the skull; mark the drilling area. Record AP and ML for the right hippocampal Schaffer collaterals and for CA1 relative to the original bregma location.

steps.title: Drill pilot holes and craniotomy
steps.instruction: Create four pilot holes at the corners of the marked locations with a dental micromotor hand drill. Perform a craniotomy of approximately 2–3 mm diameter, drilling the perimeter to remove the central bone mass while avoiding the superior sagittal sinus (located within 0.5 mm of the midline). Keep the exposed dura hydrated with saline or artificial CSF.

steps.title: Install stimulation electrode
steps.instruction: Remove the guide cannula and replace it with a bipolar stimulation electrode (Teflon‑coated stainless‑steel, 0.125 mm diameter; Advent Co., UK) mounted on the right arm of the stereotaxic frame.

steps.title: Insert stimulation electrode into Schaffer collaterals
steps.instruction: Place the electrode tip above bregma, record AP/ML, move to the calculated AP/ML coordinates, then lower the electrode holder until the tip touches the dura and record the DV value. Gently pierce the dura with a sterile small‑gauge hypodermic needle or a small hook. Advance the electrode at a rate of 1 mm every 10 s until the calculated depth is reached.

steps.title: Insert recording electrode into CA1
steps.instruction: Secure the recording electrode on the left arm of the frame, angled at 52.5°. Place its tip above bregma, record AP/ML, adjust to the CA1 coordinates, lower until the tip contacts the dura and record DV. Pierce the dura as above and advance the electrode from the left hemisphere into the right brain at 1 mm per 10 s until the desired depth is reached.

steps.title: Set up eLab recording system
steps.instruction: Turn on the laptop. Connect the eLab system to the laptop and plug the ePulse stimulator into its power adaptor (output 5.0 V, 1.55 A). In the eLab scope window set: V/D = 200 or 500 µV, T/D = 5 ms, HPF = 1 Hz, LPF = 3 kHz, Trigger = on.

steps.title: Run pattern‑test protocol
steps.instruction: In the “Experiment protocol” tab select the Pattern Test (rstT1 = 10000 µs, T2 = 150 µs, T3 = 1000 µs, T4 = 10000000 µs, N1 = 1, N2 = 100; recording time = 0 ms, trial period = 1000 ms, trial number = 100). Save the file, set stimulator current to 300 µA, start the protocol, and slowly move both electrodes within their DV ranges to locate the position that yields the maximal evoked fEPSP.

steps.title: Recovery pause
steps.instruction: Allow a minimum 30‑minute pause to let the stimulated neuronal area recover before proceeding to the next protocol.

steps.title: Run input‑output (IO) protocol
steps.instruction: Select the IO protocol (rstT1 = 10000 µs, T2 = 150 µs, T3 = 1000 µs, T4 = 10000000 µs, N1 = 1, N2 = 10; recording time = 500 ms, trial period = 10000 ms, trial number = 10). Set stimulator current to 100 µA, save as “IO100”, and start. Repeat the same steps for currents 200, 300,…, 1000 µA (increments of 100 µA), saving each file and waiting 3–5 minutes between consecutive stimulations.

steps.title: Adjust stimulus intensity
steps.instruction: After the IO curve is recorded, adjust the test‑stimulus intensity so that the evoked fEPSP slope or amplitude is approximately 50 % of the maximal response. This intensity will be used for paired‑pulse, baseline, LTP and LTD recordings.

steps.title: Run paired‑pulse protocols
steps.instruction: For each inter‑stimulus interval (10, 20, 30, 50, 70, 100 ms) select the Paired‑Pulse protocol (rstT1 = 10000 µs, T2 = 150 µs, T3 = interval µs, T4 = 10000000 µs, N1 = 2, N2 = 5; recording time = 500 ms, trial period = 10000 ms, trial number = 5). Save each as “Paired pulse <interval>”, set the stimulator current to the 50 % intensity, and start the protocol.

steps.title: Record baseline (30 min)
steps.instruction: Select the 30‑minute baseline protocol, save the file, and start. The system will record evoked fEPSPs every 5 minutes (six points total).

steps.title: Induce LTP (100 Hz)
steps.instruction: Select the LTP 100 Hz protocol (rstT1 = 10000 µs, T2 = 150 µs, T3 = 10000 µs, T4 = 10000000 µs, N1 = 50, N2 = 4; recording time = 0 ms, trial period = 10000 ms, trial number = 4). Save, start, then record a 90‑minute baseline (evoked fEPSPs every 10 minutes, nine points).

steps.title: Induce LTD (1 Hz)
steps.instruction: Select the LTD 1 Hz protocol (rstT1 = 10000 µs, T2 = 150 µs, T3 = 1000 µs, T4 = 1000000 µs, N1 = 1, N2 = 900; recording time = 0 ms, trial period = 1000 ms, trial number = 900). Save, start, then record a 30‑minute baseline as above.

steps.title: Analyze data
steps.instruction: Using eProbe/eTrace, compute: (a) IO curve – average of ten test pulses at each current (100‑1000 µA); (b) Paired‑pulse ratio – average of five pulses for each interval (10‑100 ms) and calculate % change of the second pulse relative to the first; (c) LTP/LTD – compare fEPSP slope or amplitude at baseline 90 min (post‑LTP) or 30 min (post‑LTD) to the initial 30‑min baseline. Consider induction successful when the change is ≥20 %.

description: The eProbe /eTrace analysis program allows for offline primary data detection and extraction, as well as figure export. The IO function curve is obtained by measuring the averages of ten test pulses applied at each current intensity (100-1000 µA). The amplitude and slope of the EPSP increase with higher current intensities (Fig. 7A). The paired pulses curve is obtained by measuring the averages of five test pulses applied at different interstimulus intervals (10,20,30,50,70, and100) separately (Fig. 7B). The percentage change of the second pulse compared to the first pulse is then calculated. To evaluate LTP and LTD, the EPSPs are measured before and after induction (Fig. 7C). The baseline at 30 minutes is determined by averaging the evoked fEPSPs every 5 minutes, resulting in six points on the curve. The baseline at 90 minutes is determined by averaging the evoked fEPSPs every 10 minutes, resulting in nine points on the curve.Fig. 7(A) EPSPs recorded from the IO 100-1000, with 10 different intensities labeled as a-j. (B) Paired pulses were recorded at intervals of 10, 20, 30, 50, 70 and 100 ms, labeled as a-f. (C) EPSPs were recorded before LTP / LTD induction (a), after LTP induction (b), and after LTD induction (c).Fig 7 The percentage change of the fEPSP slope and amplitude at baseline 90 minutes after LTP induction is compared to the initial baseline at 30 minutes. To evaluate LTP induction, two parameters, induction and maintenance, are assessed. Usually, induction is considered to occur when the fEPSP changes by at least 20%. For LTD evaluation, the percentage change of the fEPSP slope or amplitude at baseline 30 minutes after LTD induction is compared to the baseline at 30 minutes. Stereotaxic neurosurgery is a successful technique used on rodents for neuroscience studies.
